raw_response:
I'm 59 this year. I've been farming this land for 35 years — since I was 24. Never went to school, not even one day, but I know these 13.1 mu better than anyone. My husband and I work them together. We have two children in the city who send money home sometimes, which helps, but we're still careful with every yuan. At my age, I don't try new things. I do what worked last year, and the year before that.

**Winter wheat:** I plant in early October, around the 10th. I buy seed from the shop in town — about 30 jin per mu, same as always. Before planting, I hire the rotary tiller man to come through. Then I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Plant the wheat, irrigate it once before winter so the roots hold and it doesn't freeze. In spring, when the wheat turns green, I look at the color. If it's a bit yellow, I spread half a bag of urea per mu — that's what I've always done. Then I irrigate two more times: once when the wheat is about knee-high, and once when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide once in spring, that's usually enough.

**Summer maize:** Wheat harvest is early June. The combine comes through, and then the rush starts — sometimes we only have three or four days before we must plant the maize. I hire a couple of extra hands because my back isn't what it used to be. We till fast and plant hybrid maize seed — you can't save maize seed, everyone knows that. I put one bag of compound fertilizer in the row when planting. Maize is easier than wheat. If the rains come, I might only irrigate once, but usually I water twice: once when it's growing fast, and maybe once when it's flowering. One spray of herbicide. Harvest in late September.

I think we'll get about 420 kg per mu of wheat and 480 kg per mu of maize if the weather is normal. I'm not changing anything this year. Fertilizer is expensive again, and at my age I want a stable year, not a big gamble.
